title: Runtime evolution policy: semantic versioning, LTS streams, rollout gates, and upgrade automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Establish a clear, actionable semantic versioning and LTS strategy for the serving runtime plus a set of automated rollout gates and upgrade tooling to make upgrades predictable, low-risk, and measurable. This ticket captures the policy decisions, concrete rules for classifying changes, deprecation timelines, examples and mitigations for breaking changes, and the automation required to enforce gates (CI, canaries, rollbacks, and upgrade-assistant behavior).

Scope: runtime binary & public HTTP/SDK surface, model artifact formats (KV cache/serialized weights), on-disk state used by Private deployments, and configuration schema consumed by Dedicated/Dashboard. Excludes internal-only admin APIs and ephemeral build tooling unless they impact the public surface.

Key decisions proposed: 1) Adopt strict semver for the public runtime API (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). MAJOR => incompatible changes to request/response semantics, wire protocol, or on-disk model artifact layout. MINOR => backward-compatible features or opt-in new behaviors. PATCH => bug fixes and non-functional changes. 2) Define two support channels: stable and LTS. LTS receives critical fixes and security patches for 12 months from LTS cut; stable receives regular minor/patch updates but no long-term guarantees. 3) All MAJOR changes must go through a formal deprecation window: at least one MINOR release with feature-gated compatibility shims + two weeks of staged canaries across Dedicated customers before MAJOR tag. 4) Provide explicit machine-readable compatibility metadata in releases (compatibility-level: "runtime-major", "runtime-minor", "runtime-patch"). 5) Ship an "upgrade-assistant" CLI and CI check that validates a customer's configuration and warns about incompatible fields and deprecated flags prior to upgrade.

Concrete semver examples and guidance: - Breaking (MAJOR): change in HTTP request schema for chat completions, rename of top-level fields that SDKs parse, or change in model checkpoint format that makes older runtime unable to load newer checkpoints. Mitigation: maintain server-side negotiation for old schema for the duration of deprecation window or provide conversion tool + clear migration doc. - Additive (MINOR): new endpoint query parameter, optional output field, opt-in quantization mode. Compatible SDKs should ignore unknown fields. - Patch: bug fixes, performance improvements that do not change observable behavior, documentation updates.

Deprecation & migration timeline: - Deprecation announcement bundled with a CHANGELOG entry, PRD in Confluence, and automatic in-console alerts for Dedicated/Private customers. - Minimum deprecation window: 30 days for low-risk deprecations, 90 days for anything affecting compatibility with model artifacts or on-disk state. - Strong deprecation window (requires customer migration tooling): 180 days. - For LTS channel, deprecation timelines longer by default (90/180/365 days) based on risk class.

Rollout gates and automation: - Release artifact must pass these automated gates before promotion: unit test coverage thresholds, integration test matrix across supported model families, backward-compat test suite, performance regression suite (latency/throughput), fuzzing of request surface. - Canary plan: staged rollout anchored by metrics and traffic percentages. Default path: internal canary (1% traffic, 6 hours) -> Dedicated canaries for selected customers (0.1%–1% traffic, 24–72 hours) -> 10% traffic for 24h -> 100% gradual. - Abort criteria (examples): error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, 99th p90 latency regression > 30% over baseline, token-inference failure rate increase > 0.2%, or fail of model-loading sanity checks. Abort should trigger instant automatic rollback and create incident with runbook. - Rollback plan: immutable previous artifact available for immediate redeploy; state migration must be reversible when possible. If irreversible (e.g., on-disk format change), require migration tool and staged dual-read mode.

Upgrade tooling: - "upgrade-assistant" features: offline compatibility scanner, config diff tool, migration-helper scripts for on-disk/state changes, and a dry-run mode that simulates canary traffic. - CI integrations: a GitHub Action that runs compatibility scanner on PRs touching API/serialization code and blocks merges labeled "semver-risk" until a compatibility report is attached. - SDKs: runtime SDKs must expose runtime version negotiation helpers; SDKs pinned to major versions get warnings when newer MAJOR is published.

Observability & telemetry required: - Each release must include a compatibility-metrics dashboard showing error rates, schema errors, model-load failures, and migration success rates per customer. - Rollout jobs must emit structured events to Console traces for postmortem.

Docs & communication: - Pattern: initial RFC -> engineering spec -> deprecation announcement (Confluence) -> public CHANGELOG entry -> Console notification -> targeted email/Slack for Reserved customers. - Provide migration guides with code snippets, automated conversion scripts (where feasible), and sample rollbacks.

Success criteria: - No unplanned MAJOR rollbacks in the first 6 months after policy enforcement. - 95% of upgrades that pass automated gates complete canary stages without manual intervention. - Reduction in post-upgrade support tickets attributable to semver incompatibility by 75% vs baseline.

Out of scope for this ticket: specific SDK language patches (tracked separately), marketplace/partner integration cadence, and policy for third-party model artifact formats beyond our curated catalog.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clear semver decision text in this ticket and a one-page summary published to Confluence.
- Compatibility test suite added to CI that fails pull requests tagged with breaking-change without an attached migration plan.
- upgrade-assistant v0.1 implemented with dry-run and compatibility-scan features and a GitHub Action integration.
- Canary rollout playbook documented and added to runtime runbooks with abort thresholds and automated rollback steps.
- Console notification flow for deprecation announcements is implemented and tested against a Dedicated sandbox customer.
